entries.subject: NOIRLab noao-m27
entries.finding: M27, NGC 6853, Dumbbell Nebula: a color composite from the Kitt Peak 2.1-meter telescope; its page names no filters; 1750 × 1500 px over 8.90 × 7.63 arcmin. The file's embedded sky tags, used as they are: 0.3053 arcsec per pixel, north 2.1° left of vertical, the frame's centre at 299.9038269°, 22.7212155°. Not measured against Gaia here.

entries.subject: The shape of the Dumbbell Nebula
entries.finding: The picture is flat. Depth needs the nebula's shape as a paper gives it, which is how the Ring and the Owl took theirs. For the Dumbbell, Meaburn et al. (2005) measure the kinematics and call the bright shell quasi-ellipsoidal or barrel-shaped, expanding at 35 km/s along its minor axis, but print no tilt of its axis to the line of sight. Kwok et al. (2008), The True Shapes of the Dumbbell and the Ring, is closed access and was not read.
entries.revisitWhen: A paper that prints the shell's axes and its tilt is read.

entries.subject: Stars in the picture
entries.finding: The photograph first kept its stars, which stood on the nebula's plane whatever their own distances. The Nebula Lab's NOX removes them and keeps the nebula's structure. The glow of the brightest stars remains. A second pass over a quarter-size copy takes saturated stars, but on this picture it also took real nebula, so it is not used. The galaxies' glow fill, which needs a star table, erased nebula around the stars that light it and is not used on nebulae.
